As of writing, I've played every Disgaea game except for 3 and D2. I'm rather experienced with this series now, so I'm happy to share why I think everyone should give Disgaea 2 a try.

Demon Overlord Zenon has turned all the humans in Veldime into demons, and it's up to the last human in the world, Adell, to stop him. However, a summoning ritual ends up summoning Zenon's daughter Rozalin instead! The story itself is not groundbreaking or anything, but I enjoyed the cast quite a bit. The best part is seeing the relationship between Adell and Rozalin develop as the game progresses. There's also returning characters from the first game, but I wouldn't say you're required to play Disgaea 1 first in order to enjoy this one.

Disgaea 2 builds off of the original game's strategy RPG gameplay and improves it to the point where it feels much better to play. Healers actually earn EXP for healing this time! The Item World is also much more functional than the one in the first game. There are also lots of new classes to try out, and a new weapon type for monsters that actually helps make them viable team members. This version also includes all the DLC characters from the PSP release and the additional Axel Mode. The game is grindy, as to be expected of a Nippon Ichi Software game, but if you're like me you'll enjoy diving into the Item World for hours and leveling up.

El dia de hoy buscaremos venganza, toca hablar de Disgaea 2, específicamente del port de PC, lanzado el 30 de enero de 2017 para la plataforma de steam, este juego fue desarrollado por Nippon Ichi Software, es un juego RPG de estrategia, y no nos tardemos mas en ver su sinopsis:

Para salvar a su familia, Adell intenta invocar a Zenon, pero invoca por error a Rozalin, la hija del Overlord. Ambos emprenden un viaje lleno de humor y estrategia para encontrar a Zenon

->La historia de Adell y su búsqueda por levantar la maldición de Zenon, es una genialidad de principio a fin, conforme avanzamos en la trama se nos revelan muchísimos giros de tuerca, conocemos a profundidad a los personajes, por que Adell nunca rompe promesas, las inseguridades de Rozalin que la misma desconocía, Axel y su complejo de Héroe oscuro, cada personaje que conocemos de la trama es sumamente interesante y están bastante cuidados.

En conclusión Disgaea 2 es una mejora completa a su antecesor, tanto en jugabilidad como en historia, es mucho mas accesible al publico pero que si realmente quieres sacarle todo el potencial debes pasar muchas horas de juego, por mi parte se lleva un 8 de 10.

While I do believe this game is better than Disgaea 1, aside from the plot which explicitly pads itself to a nauseating degree after chapter 8, I feel like Disgaea 2 failed to make level-grinding fun or interesting. At a point, I was at a place in the story where the average enemy level was 75, and, having used the reincarnation mechanic to reset all my characters at least once (upwards of around 3 times a unit) before, my entire team was around level 20-50. That's not the problem - I just needed to just level up my team, but there aren't many adequate grinding stages. The ones I deemed accessible I had already used around 70 times, and there's only so many times I can put myself through rolling a kill via team attack against the same enemies. So, I just quit and moved onto Disgaea 5, which I heard is meant to be the best, mechanically. I would've brute forced it, but the stage I was stuck on was brute-proof (that horrendous no-ranged-attack geo-covered stage). While I do like the added depth to the Item World (pirates, mystery rooms, court), Dark Council system (fun bills, removing the promotion exams), better weapon balancing (lances feel good to use now), mana potions, etc., the lack of grinding support makes me feel retroactively boned for engaging with the game's reincarnation mechanics.

Disgaea 2 PC is a loud, chaotic, and surprisingly thoughtful strategy RPG that embraces excess in the best possible way. It mixes turn-based tactical battles with a goofy demon-world story, and the result feels like a game that’s constantly winking at you while still taking its core systems seriously. Even years after its original release, the PC version remains a solid entry point for anyone curious about the series’ reputation for “numbers go up” madness.

The story follows Adell, a rare human living in a cursed land where everyone else has been turned into a demon. He’s stubborn, straightforward, and plays the perfect foil to the cast of eccentric villains and unlikely allies that pile into the party. The writing leans heavily into humor, but it’s not just random silliness—there’s a steady theme about identity, pride, and responsibility that gives the narrative more heart than you might expect.

Where the game truly shines is combat. Battles take place on grid-based maps with height differences, terrain considerations, and positioning that matters a lot once the difficulty ramps up. You’ll be throwing characters, chaining attacks with teammates, and setting up multi-step turns that feel like solving a puzzle. It’s easy to start with simple moves and then gradually discover tactics that turn a messy skirmish into a clean, satisfying win.

Customization is practically the main course. You can build a team from many classes, reincarnate characters to reshape their growth, and develop gear to absurd levels. The Item World—a series of randomly generated floors inside your equipment—is the perfect example of Disgaea’s loop: dive in “just for a few floors,” emerge an hour later with stronger items and a longer to-do list. Progress is addictive because you’re always one clever idea away from a bigger power spike.

That said, Disgaea 2 PC is not shy about grind, and it expects you to enjoy that process. If you prefer tightly paced campaigns with minimal side systems, the game can feel like it’s pulling you away from the story every time you get comfortable. Menus and mechanics come fast, and while the basics are clear enough, mastering the deeper layers takes patience and experimentation.

The PC version runs well and benefits from the convenience of modern platforms, making it easier to jump in for short sessions or long marathons. Visually, the sprites and animations are charming rather than flashy, and the soundtrack fits the mischievous tone nicely. Some aspects still show their age—interface quirks and repeated animations can wear thin—but the overall presentation holds up because the gameplay is doing the heavy lifting.

In the end, Disgaea 2 PC is best described as a tactical RPG playground. It rewards curiosity, encourages absurd strategies, and gives you the tools to break it wide open if you’re willing to learn its rules. If you want a strategy game with personality, endless progression, and a sense that the developers intentionally designed it for people who love optimizing, it’s an easy recommendation—just be ready to lose track of time in the Item World.

[b] Я больно много думаю о DISGAEA 2. [/b]
С виду обычная SRPG да ещё и гриндилка про узколобого деревенского парня Аделя, который пытается одолеть владыку преисподней Зенона. Но не чтобы стать великим и могучим владыкой, а вернуть своей семье и жителям деревни прежний человеческий облик. Мы бы так и смотрели за занудной авантюрой правильного мальчика Аделя, если бы не одно но — [b] это DISGAEA[/b], мир, в котором творится дурдом. И во второй части произошла одна ошибка, из-за которой я полюбил её.
«Парень собирался призвать Зенона, великого повелителя преисподней, одержимый желанием одолеть его всю жизнь, посреди своей деревни и отмудохать его. Вот так просто. Призвать из котла при помощи мамы... И тут произошёл промах».
Ошибка, которая на самом деле не просто спасла Аделя, а стала началом целого путешествия, о котором я думаю по сей день, и зовут её — Розалин.
Я, честно, не ожидал ничего от игры, и это сыграло свою роль. Мне понравилось, как DISGAEA мило выглядела по скриншотам и потянула на моём старом ноутбуке. Я поиграл в первую часть, только она вообще меня не зацепила, но я решил дать шанс и поиграть во вторую часть, ведь она сильно и не связана с первой.

[b] А что я получил в итоге? [/b]

Со временем игра просто [b]уничтожила [/b]мои ожидания о том, что она будет скучной, своими зрелищными боями, скорее даже втянула меня в эту динамичность. Анимировано всё и так круто, а потом всё становится настолько гиперболизировано динамичным, что было не оторваться. Я был зависим от этой гриндилки. Если всё прокачать как надо — то бои становятся не столько головоломками, сколько absolute cinema благодаря различным навыкам у персонажей. Точно, персонажи — это прям самый сок. Я намеренно взял себе героев из дополнений сразу, чтобы украсить бои. Забегая вперёд — это было не самым правильным, но самым красивым решением, и я ни о чём не жалел.
Сюжет такой приятный, персонажи такие красочные и красивые, что я аж соскучился по ним и их приключениям. Следить за постоянной враждой и отношениями между Аделем и Розалин было интереснее, чем попытки инфантильного пацана стать оверлордом. Первая часть была как будто про элиту, а вторая опускает нас в обычный мир и показывает одной из таких элит (самой дочке Зенона) — каково живётся низкоранговым.

Хоть я и до сих пор не прошёл её до конца, но Disgaea 2 заняла место в моём сердце и греет его каждый раз, как вспоминаю об этом чудаковатом и гротескном мире, полном владык и драк. Новости по телику, её ведущие, попытки бывшей звезды вернуть свою славу, снять зрелищные сцены, постоянные драки ради того, чтобы стать великим повелителем — мир живой, и, короче, в нём происходит настоящая шумиха. Disgaea 2 PC brings one of Nippon Ichi Software’s most beloved tactical RPGs to a modern platform, offering a sprawling mix of comedy, strategic depth, and limitless character growth. At its center is the story of Adell, a determined young man living in the cursed world of Veldime, where nearly every resident has been transformed into a demon by the mysterious overlord Zenon. Adell’s stubborn heroism drives the narrative—he’s the only one unaffected by the curse, and he vows to confront Zenon directly. His journey quickly becomes tangled in Netherworld politics, clashing personalities, and comedic misunderstandings, especially once the sheltered Rozalin enters the picture. The story blends serious themes with the series’ trademark silliness, giving players a mix of sentimentality and slapstick chaos. It rarely aims for emotional complexity but remains consistently entertaining thanks to its quirky cast and comedic timing.

The real core of Disgaea 2 lies in its tactical gameplay and dizzying mechanical depth. Each battle unfolds on an isometric grid, where positioning, team synergy, and environmental manipulation matter just as much as raw stats. Geo Panels—colored tiles that grant positive or negative effects—turn many battles into puzzles where a clever player can swing entire encounters by destroying or rearranging these effects. The combat system encourages experimentation, offering a range of classes, monster types, combo attacks, and weapon skills. Even early battles give players glimpses of the game’s long-term potential, and as the roster grows, managing a varied team becomes its own rewarding challenge.

One of the franchise’s defining features, and one fully intact in this PC release, is the freedom to grind, tweak, and rebuild characters in almost limitless ways. Leveling to 9999 is not an exaggeration but a goal the game expects players to pursue. Reincarnation allows you to reset a character to level one while retaining improved stats, turning progression into a long-term investment rather than a linear climb. The notorious Item World—a dungeon that exists inside each piece of equipment—adds an entire parallel progression system where items level up alongside your characters. It’s a mechanic that feels absurd at first, yet it becomes the backbone of late-game optimization, offering randomly generated floors full of enemies, bonuses, and strategic surprises.

The PC version includes the expanded content from previous console editions, such as additional characters and side scenarios, making it the most complete version of Disgaea 2 available. While the port functions well overall, it does retain some of the technical limits of its original era. Visuals rely heavily on upscaled 2D sprites and modest environments, which may feel dated, especially compared to the crisp HD look of newer entries in the series. The UI and performance are reliable but not extensively modernized, and the mouse-and-keyboard controls, while usable, don’t entirely replace the comfort of a controller. Still, the port remains stable, and the inclusion of extra content adds considerable value.

Where Disgaea 2 truly excels is in giving players an astonishing amount of freedom. You can focus on the story and enjoy a relatively linear path, or you can dive headfirst into min-maxing, experimenting with character builds, and exploring the labyrinthine post-game. This freedom, however, comes with a warning: the game thrives on grinding. For players who enjoy incremental power growth, absurd stat inflation, and squeezing every advantage out of complex systems, this is a paradise. But for those who prefer tightly balanced strategy or narrative-driven progression, the endless grind may feel overwhelming or repetitive. Disgaea 2 embraces excess—and expects you to embrace it too.

Ultimately, Disgaea 2 PC succeeds as both a nostalgic revival and a robust tactical RPG in its own right. Its humor, charm, and mechanical ambition stand out even years after its original release. The story may not break new ground, and the visuals show their age, but the gameplay’s depth, replayability, and sheer creative freedom make it a standout entry in the genre. For players who love strategy games that let them break the rules, push systems to their limits, and build unstoppable teams through dedication and experimentation, Disgaea 2 PC is an endlessly rewarding experience.

[h1]⚠️Potenzielle Triggerpunkte!⚠️[/h1]

[h1]🎮Gameplay🎮[/h1]

[b][u]Praktische Einrichtungen und Rasterstrategie[/u][/b]

Dreh- und Angelpunkt aller Spieleraktivitäten in Disgaea 2 ist der [b]Hub[/b], in dem man neben Einkaufen auch die Missionsauswahl finden kann, von der aus man (fast) jede bereits gespielte sowie anstehende Mission ansteuern kann. Die [b]Missionen[/b] in Disgaea 2 laufen als rundenbasierte Kämpfe auf einem Rasterfeld ab, das neben höheren und niedrigeren Ebenen auch [b]Geo-Panels[/b] enthalten kann, die unterschiedlichste Effekte haben können, wie eine Erhöhung der Statuswerte oder die Verursachung von Schaden. [b]Charaktere[/b] müssen über einen speziellen Punkt „beschworen“ werden und man ist auf 10 Charaktere beschränkt. Charaktere haben außerdem jeder einen Radius, in dem sie sich bewegen können, Höhen, die sie überwinden können, und Entfernungen, über die sie andere Charaktere [b]werfen[/b] können. Gerade letzteres spielt später eine große Rolle, da einige Bereiche eines Levels zu Fuß nicht erreichbar sind.


[b][u]Strategischer Tiefgang oder Puzzle?- Fähigkeiten[/u][/b] 

Charaktere haben logischerweise auch [b]Fähigkeiten[/b], die sie ausmachen. Einige sind vielseitig einsetzbar, wieder andere nur sehr bedingt, da sie eine genaue Positionierung erfordern und manche andere Felder ebenfalls frei sein müssen, da der Charakter sich entweder während des Skills umherbewegt, am Ende woanders steht oder der Gegner eine andere Position einnimmt. Das kann nützlich sein, aber auch hinderlich. Der Spieler ist nicht gezwungen, alle Aktionen in einer Runde [b]durchzuplanen[/b], da man Charaktere bewegen und ihnen Aktionen zuweisen kann, bevor man den Zug dann ausführt. Aktionen, die während der Planung noch möglich waren, aber im anschließenden Prozess dann nicht mehr, werden nicht ausgeführt und der Charakter behält seine Aktion für die Runde. Jeder Charakter hat zudem eine Bewegung und eine Aktion pro Runde. Eine spezielle Form des Angriffs ist der Teamangriff, bei dem nebeneinander stehende Charaktere gemeinsam einen Gegner angreifen, um so mehr Schaden zu verursachen.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3519741557

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3523567872


[b][u]Mikromanagement und Grind[/u][/b]

In Disgaea 2 gibt es mehr Möglichkeiten, einen Charakter zu stärken, als ihn nur zu leveln. Eine davon ist das Erschaffen von [b]Untergebenen[/b], die ihrem Meister durch Level-Ups Bonusattribute einbringen und von denen jener Meister nichtklassenspezifische Skills lernen kann. Eine andere ist die [b]Reinkarnation[/b], bei der eine Einheit auf Level eins zurückgesetzt wird, um mit höheren Basisattributen noch mal zu starten und am Ende noch stärker zu sein als vorher.

Lo más curioso de este juego es que tiene a un protagonista serio y con metas normalitas, cuestión atípica en un Disgaea. Por lo mismo el tono es generalmente más serio, aunque no por ello dejen de lado cualquier momento para hacer reír. De hecho Axel, que es algo así como el rival del protagonista en este juego, es quien mantiene mayormente ese lado. Aunque Axel siempre es presentado de forma tan cómica que en lo personal me cansé de verlo, con todo y su historia incluida. Esta clase de personaje tipo "pierrot" (cómico por fuera pero con un trasfondo triste o trágico) funcionaban mejor conmigo durante la adolescencia. Creces y pierden toda su gracia si no están bien hechos.

Por lo mismo -y estos son spoilers, de cierta manera- cuando al terminar el juego y entrar al modo Axel ya no quise continuar jugando. Escribo esto habiendo terminado tan solo el primer par de niveles en el modo Axel. No porque odie al tipo, sino porque los personajes principales de la historia principal se desvanecen en este modo y sentí que todo ese tiempo en el item world grindeando subpoenas, objetos y experiencia en el 9-2 fue tirado a la basura, pues me quitaron una parte importante de mis fuerzas, fue como un golpe al estómago que te deja sin aire.

Por cierto, los subpoenas son la parte más curiosa que trae este juego a la mesa. No los he visto en los títulos siguientes y es curioso. La idea es que subir mucho tus stats o matar muchos enemigos se considera un crimen y te citan con el juez, que está en el item world de un "subpoena", un objeto que recibes. Al entrar con el juez cada personaje que atravesó el portal recibe 2 felonías. El aspecto más importante de tener felonías es que aumenta la cantidad de experiencia en un porcentaje igual al número de felonías que tengas (2 felonías es 2%, por decir). Es un sistema curioso que facilita grindear a futuro.

El grindeo fue para mí la peor parte. El único sitio decente de entre todos los mapas principales para grindear se encuentra hasta el capítulo 9, ya en la recta final. Por otro lado, hay una zona que puedes desbloquear más tarde con la cual también puedes grindear, aunque toma más tiempo. Tal vez en los mapas del modo Axel encuentres algo, pero como dije, el robo de mis personajes se llevó por el drenaje todas las ganas de continuar.

No por eso significa que el juego sea malo ni nada por el estilo. Es entretenido y la historia hace que te enganches en el desarrollo de la relación entre Adell y Rozalin. De todos los Disgaea que he jugado hasta ahora (del 1 al 5 sin contar D2) la parejita en este juego ha sido de lo más memorable en términos de personajes. Lástima que no pueda decir lo mismo del resto. O tienen diseños poco memorables o los personajes por sí mismos son poco interesantes. La única que se salva, para mí, fue Yukimaru, una ninja kawaii que termina todas sus oraciones en "de gozaru". Pero solo eso. Ah, y Axel, que tiene mil cameos en juegos futuros.

Como juego para entrar a la experiencia que es grindear durante horas no recomendaría Disgaea 2. Para eso mejor Disgaea 5. Por otro lado, como un jrpg sólido con mil mecánicas distintas y una historia que tira tanto por el lado cómico como el lado serio, recomiendo este título a creces.

These days it feels like we are in a time where games fight for your screen time by means of weekly grinds and missable rewards. The games need to be everlasting and so do the slow paced stories.

WIth that in mind it's pretty nice to go back to a classic game like this, and doing so after last playing ~7+ years ago certainly gets me thinking about that comparison.

With this you get a game with a story that has plenty humorous moments (though mind that this is a 2006 game) but also has the occasional serious moment, the SRPG gameplay may not be the most tactical but offers plenty freedom in building up your party (Nothing stopping you from building a party of moths or making your mages martial artists, efficiency aside) and while the terrain is not much to write home about the work put into the character sprites is pretty good. (And don't worry, you can turn off the blurry character filter!)

And then when you finish the story... what now?
Well here's a postgame that'll easily burn hundreds of hours if you allow it, with plenty enough stuff to do to either power up your party or do the former more efficiently (it doesn't just stop with reaching level 9999!), and plenty bosses along the way to act as goalposts to justify your grind.
It's also one of those cases where you can really watch numbers go up- especially when you upgrade a piece of equipment and toss it onto your well trained unit(s).

As far as modern releases go in this franchise, while missing out on modern QoLs that you'll see in newer games still is a significant upgrade over the first game in everything but D1's memorable story/characters, and is not a bad starting point (especially if you're in the mood for something from the 2000s PS2 era, I like the 'SD sprite' style over the HD/3D styles from later games anyway).

For the occasional mood to unwind with a game that offers you hours of grinding rather than demanding you to do it today and again next week, this is certainly a good way to feed that.
It's like working on a bit of a project [strike]while you're procrastinating your actual projects and tasks[/strike].
